BEEKMAN ARMS
"America's Oldest Inn"
Rhinebeck, New York
The Beekman Arms, first known as Traphagen's Tavern, has long been a resting place for the hungry and weary travelers of the old Albany Post Road. Established in 1766, the Beekman Arms is credited by the historians and the American Hotel Association with being the "Oldest Hotel in America" in continuous operation. In its beginning, the Beekman Arms was a one story stone building
constructed with a dual purpose in mind: to provide bed and board for the traveler, and to serve as a shelter for the local residents against Indian attack. Later, during the Revolutionary War, General Washington often watched his troops drilling in the square from a corner window while he awaited for his couriers to arrive with news. Many other famous persons of past and present have also visited the old Inn. Included are General Montgomery, Alexander Hamilton, Aaron Burr, DeWitt Clinton, Benedict
Arnold, Martin Van Buren, Vice President Levi P. Morton and more recent times, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Astronaut James Lovell, Governor Nelson Rockefeller, as well as many present personalitites from the stage and screen. The Beekman Arms invites you, too, to partake of its authentic early American atmosphere with its hearty fare and comfortable rooms. Located at the Sepasco Trail and King's Highway (now State 308 and U.S. Route Nine), the Beekman Arms serves the public every day
of the year in the traditional manner of fine inn-keeping.

Porc - 40 m. par livre et decouper en tranches minces.
Cotes de Boeuf - 15 m. livre, mais avoir soin de la laisser reposer 20 m. a l'etuvee.
Poulet Reine - 15 m. par livre. Decouper en morceaux.
Filet de Boeuf - 14 m. par livre.  Laisser reposer 15 m. a l'etuve, le decoupage se pratique mieux.  Couper le filet en tranches assez minces.
Poulet de Grain - 20 m. de cuisson et decouper en quatre.
Roastbeef - 12 a 15 m. suivant la forme du roastbeef
Canard - 15 m. par livre. Se decoupe en filets pour la poitrine et en morceaux pour les cuisses.
Roti de Veau - 35 a 40 m. par livre. Le decoupage se fait en tranches plus epaisses que pour le boeuf. Servir bien cuit.
Dinde - Il faut I h. 30 pour le dindonneau et environ 2 heures a 2 h. 20 pour les gros dindons.
Gigot de Mouton - 15 m. par livre. Decouper egalement en tranches larges, ni trop epaisses, ni trop minces.
Pigeons - De 300 a 350 grammes, 25 a 30 m. de cuisson.
Selle de Mouton - 15 m. par livre. Decouper dans le sens de la largeur apres avoir detache les os des deux cotes de la selle.
Pintade - 3/4 d'heure de cuisson. Decouper comme le poulet reine.
